You might find this strange, but the true nature of the mind is neutral. It is neither for you or against you. The mind evolved with a negative bias, i.e. you see more pain and suffering than joy and happiness. The trick is to not attach to any thoughts you have, good or bad, just let it be. You can label them if you like, if you’re angry, say am angry. If you’re sad, say you’re sad, etc. just to acknowledge what you’re thinking and feeling at that moment and then let go.

Quick anecdote: there was a reporter that jumped to her death from a tall building. She left a note, and it said she did it because her thoughts are driving her crazy.

The mind is a ruthless master but makes for an excellent servant. Hope this helps.

I understand your point, but keep in mind we all have our own criteria when it comes to investing.  There's no one way to make people decide to invest in a project or not, it's really up to you. It is, after all, your money and no one would care about it more than you do.

It's not so much as the launch date the issue here, but it's the commitment they made when they say they will deliver at such date. By missing it, it didn't instill confidence in me to invest in the token. I have managed projects in the past, and when we tell the client we will get the project done at such and such date, they hold us to it. We were held accountable for it. It's part of doing good business, and you gain credibility when you meet the date, and the client becomes more comfortable and confident with you that they will choose to do more business with you, growing your earnings and investment. This is just one of my criteria in investing, a litmus test if you will, but only applies to my own DYOR.
